sense: a series that comes round again

evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.52: a planet eundem duodecim signōrum orbem annīs duodecim cōnficit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Properly a circle or ring, and so the round that a star or a course of events goes through and comes back from: orbem cōnficere, to complete a cycle. Its other everyday senses are a disc or round surface, and the world (orbis terrārum).

terms.gloss: a going round, a revolution; a periodic return
evidence: Cels. 3.5: the periodic return of a fever (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: More often a way round, a circuit or detour (Caes., Liv.).

terms.gloss: alternation, the coming round of each in turn
terms.comment: For things that take turns, as day and night or the seasons, rather than a single round.

terms.gloss: a cycle (in astronomy and the calendar)
terms.comment: A Greek word, late and technical: the Easter cycle, the lunar cycle. Lewis & Short marks its y as common, so it is left unmarked.

phrases.latin: mīrīque sunt orbēs et quasi circuitūs in rēbus pūblicīs commūtātiōnum et vicissitūdinum
phrases.english: and there are remarkable cycles and, as it were, rounds of change and alternation in states

phrases.latin: quem vērō astrōrum ōrdinēs, quem diērum noctiumque vicissitūdinēs … nōn grātum esse cōgunt
phrases.english: but someone whom the order of the stars, the alternation of days and nights … do not make grateful
